value.body: A two-year postgraduate degree in computer science or information technology, taken after a BCA or a B.Sc with computer science or mathematics. It covers algorithms, systems, networks, databases and electives such as machine learning, usually with a project or dissertation.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's in computer science, IT, BCA or a B.Sc with mathematics or computer science, usually with a minimum percentage set by the university. Admission is through CUET-PG at participating universities, a university's own entrance test, or merit.

value.title: At a glance
items: The M.Sc leans more to theory and research; the MCA leans more to applications. Both lead to similar software roles.
The M.Sc is a common route to UGC-NET, college teaching and a PhD.
For industry jobs, projects, internships and coding skill weigh heavily alongside the degree.
Fees differ widely between government universities and private colleges.
